messages.subject: point mean prediction = all great;      distribution prediction = much worst.     - Help!
parts:
Hello,

I am predicting the components of a weighted sum of lognormal distributions

================================================================

e.g., y = LOGnormal(..,..) * 0.5 + LOGnormal(..,..) * 0.1 + LOGnormal(..,..) * 0.4
...
...

================================================================

If I try to predict only the means as point values

for(p in 1:P)  temp[p] = log_proportion[s,p] + alpha_mean[g,p];
y[g,s] ~ lognormal( log_sum_exp(temp), sigma);

the result is reliable and the convergence good




If I try to predict not just the mean but also the standard deviation of those components

alpha[s,g] ~ lognormal(alpha_mean[g], alpha_sd[g]);                     
           
for(p in 1:P)  temp[p] = log_proportion[s,p] + log_alpha[s,g,p];                    
y[g,s] ~ lognormal( log_sum_exp(temp), sigma);                           

the result is somewhat close to the right one but  I can't get the chains to converge. Could you please suggest what might be wrong, in the model or in my fundamental assumptions?

=====================================

data {
    int<lower=1> G;
    int<lower=1> S;                                                                                  // number of cases
    int<lower=1> P;                                                                                  // number of cases
    vector[P] proportion[S];                                                                      // predictor (covariate)
    vector[S] y[G];                                                                                    // outcome (variate)
    real alpha_mean_mean;                                                                    // means of the means
    real alpha_mean_sd;                                                                         // sd of the means
    real alpha_sd_beta;                                                                           // gamma parameter of the distribution of standard deviations
    real alpha_sd_alpha;                                                                         // gamma parameter of the distribution of standard deviations
}
transformed data{
    vector[P] log_proportion[S];                                                                                                   // proportions log transform for speed
    for(s in 1:S) log_proportion[s] = log(proportion[s]);
}
parameters {
    real<lower=0.00001, upper=100> sigma;                                           // prediction noise
    vector<lower=1>[P] alpha[S,G];                                                          // unknown true value for each mix
    vector<lower=0.00001, upper=10>[P] alpha_sd[G];                           // prior scale
    vector<lower=0, upper=100>[P] alpha_mean[G];                               // prior location
   
}
transformed parameters{
        vector<lower=0>[P] log_alpha[S,G];                                                                                    // value log transform for speed
        for(g in 1:G) for(s in 1:S) log_alpha[s,g] = log(alpha[s,g]);
}
model {
    vector[P] temp;
   
    for(g in 1:G) for(s in 1:S) {
        alpha[s,g] ~ lognormal(alpha_mean[g], alpha_sd[g]);                      // get distribution of each component
           
        for(p in 1:P)  temp[p] = log_proportion[s,p] + log_alpha[s,g,p];        // make weighted sum
        y[g,s] ~ lognormal( log_sum_exp(temp), sigma);                              // aveluate sum against observed mix
        }
       
    for(g in 1:G) alpha_sd[g] ~ gamma(alpha_sd_alpha, alpha_sd_beta);                 // priors
    for(g in 1:G) alpha_mean[g] ~ normal(alpha_mean_mean,alpha_mean_sd);       // priors
    sigma ~ cauchy(0, 2);                                                                                            // priors
   
}
